game: ATL @ NO Week 4 2026 (morning of kickoff; spread/total/weather/inactives not in pack)

script.base: No spread saved, so script is from form only. Atlanta should lean on Bijan Robinson (66 car, 349 yds, 5.29 YPC, ~22/g) and Brian Robinson (30/132) against a Saints run defense allowing 4.85 YPC and 11 runs of 10+, with LBs Kaden Elliss, Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings out. New Orleans cannot feature the run: Kamara is at 2.83 YPC (18/51) behind Etienne (30/128), and Atlanta allows 3.12 YPC with only 2 runs of 10+. Tyler Shough's offense throws to Olave (36 tgt), Vele (22) and Juwan Johnson (19). Base is competitive, Atlanta run-leaning if tied or ahead, Saints pass-volume either way.
script.flip1: Saints score first through Olave (12 tgt/g, 472 air yards). Atlanta abandons the run, Bijan and Brian Robinson carries stall, Penix volume rises toward London. Johnson and Olave targets stay live; any Atlanta rush over dies.
script.flip2: Atlanta gets up and clocks it, or the game is a low-play slog (total unknown). Bijan carries rise late; London stalls because Atlanta is already -0.58 EPA/db when not blitzed and New Orleans blitzes only 30%. A true blowout the other way pulls Saints starters and both receiving overs die together.

injury_fallout: Pack official report only; final inactives not saved. NO OUT: LB Kaden Elliss (calf), LB Carl Granderson (ankle), LB Anfernee Jennings (knee). That is a depleted Saints front seven, so Atlanta rushers (Bijan, Brian Robinson) gain lanes; no offensive Saint is OUT, so no forced skill-position replacement. NO TE Noah Fant is Questionable (abdomen) after 12 tgt/66 yds — if he later sits, Juwan Johnson (already 19/173, the TE1) and to a lesser extent Devaughn Vele absorb looks; do not price Fant as out. Pete Werner Q (shoulder) is another Saints LB, not confirmed out. ATL Q only: DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) would trim Atlanta pressure if he sits (helps Shough), LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) and LB Yasir Abdullah (illness) would soften seam coverage for Johnson if they sit. None of the Atlanta tags are Out. Source: nflverse injury block in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Proxy only: Saints blitz 30%, Atlanta blitz 21%.
matchup.pressure: Atlanta EPA/db is -0.00 vs blitz and -0.58 vs no blitz, so Penix is worse on the 70% of snaps New Orleans does not blitz. Saints EPA/db is -0.12 vs blitz and +0.11 vs no blitz; Atlanta's 21% blitz rate leaves Shough in the better look most of the time. Granderson out may further cut Saints pressure, which hurts any Atlanta pass-under and does not create a pressure-boosted checkdown story for New Orleans.
matchup.bleeds: Atlanta bleeds the middle (9.45 YPA on 20 att) and has allowed 12 passes of 20+ (135 yds); perimeter YPA is fine (left 5.86 on 50, right 5.63 on 60). Atlanta run defense does not bleed (3.12 YPC, 2 runs of 10+). Saints bleed the run (4.85 YPC, 11 runs of 10+) and are softer to the left (7.55 YPA on 38) than the right (6.02 on 43); only 6 passes of 20+ (109).
matchup.overlap: Saints primary is Olave (36/117 targets, 30.8%, 472 air, 13.1 aDOT) into Atlanta's explosive-pass allowance, not into a soft perimeter YPA. Johnson (19 tgt, 103 air, 5.4 aDOT) is the cleaner overlap with the actual YPA hole (middle 9.45). Atlanta primary London (19 tgt, 274 yds, but 29 and 51 in two of three games) has no clean Saints hole and a poor non-blitz EPA environment.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Juwan Johnson has cleared 46.5 in every game (54, 66, 53) on intermediate targets, and he is the Saints skill player who actually attacks the only soft spot on Atlanta's pass defense, the middle at 9.45 YPA, in a game where Atlanta's run wall should keep Shough throwing.
edge_players.must_be_true: Johnson keeps a full TE1 route share (about 6 targets, as in the 19-target three-game sample), Shough plays, and the game produces a normal pass volume rather than a 40-play slog. Fant staying Questionable is fine; he does not need to sit.
edge_players.kills_it: A low-play slog, Etienne/Kamara checkdowns stealing the seam (Etienne already has 13 targets), or Deablo and Abdullah both playing and erasing the middle after a 20-attempt sample. One quiet game under his 53-yard floor loses a number only 6.5 yards below that floor.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost because this was a low-play Atlanta control game, not a Saints throw day. Bijan (already 22 carries a game) and Brian Robinson ran it at a Saints front missing Elliss, Granderson and Jennings, Shough never reached a full pass count, and the checkdowns that did come went to Etienne (13 targets, -9 air) instead of Johnson, so 46.5 died even after a 53-yard floor in a three-game sample. Olave was the 86-yard version, not the 182: 472 air yards and a 13.1 aDOT mean a few incompletions finish him at 70-85, and Atlanta's perimeter YPA was never the hole. Fant played and took seam targets. Deablo and Abdullah both played, and the middle 9.45 YPA on only 20 throws was noise. No total was saved, so the slog was always live, and the two legs die together if New Orleans does not throw.
slip_story: One story only: New Orleans has to throw because Atlanta allows 3.12 YPC and 2 runs of 10+, so stack Olave (primary, explosives) with Johnson (middle YPA). Do not add a total under, a London or Pitts over, or a Bijan rush over — those need Atlanta to trail or the 194-yard spikes to repeat. Kamara rush+rec under fits the same run-wall story but was dropped on the lean-vs-market rule, not slipped. No TD legs, one market per player, two legs.
